name: pari
desc: Computer algebra system designed for fast computations in number theory
why: A number theory computer algebra system with its own interactive language, a real days-off math playground.

brief.what_it_is: PARI/GP is a free, cross-platform computer algebra system aimed at fast number theory: factorization, algebraic number theory, elliptic curves, modular forms, L-functions. It also covers matrices, polynomials, power series, algebraic numbers and many transcendental functions, plus numerical summation and integration. You type expressions into the interactive shell gp, or write scripts in GP's own language. Results print to the terminal. PARI is also available as a C library.
brief.why_it_exists: The project has been developed since the early 1980s at the University of Bordeaux as a fast tool for computing in number theory. The homepage frames it as a fast number-theory system that is also free software under the GPL.
brief.how_it_works: The core is a C library that does the heavy arithmetic. gp is an interactive shell on top of it that exposes those functions. GP is the name of gp's scripting language. gp2c, a GP-to-C compiler, turns GP scripts into C and loads the compiled functions back into gp transparently; the homepage says these typically run 3 or 4 times faster, but gp2c only understands a subset of GP.
brief.install_notes: The brew formula installs gp, gp-2.17, gphelp and tex2mail. Brew's caveat says graphical plotting needs X11, installed with: brew install --cask xquartz. I did not see other setup steps on the pages I read. The docs include an Installation Guide (PDF) for UNIX-type platforms.
brief.standout: It is a real research-grade CAS with a small interactive language, and the homepage lists a C library, a compiler from its own script language to C, and a browser version to try. The author's own framing is that it is for fast computation rather than symbolic breadth.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage announces PARI-2.19.0 as the new major release, dated 2026-09-28. It also lists a 25th Atelier PARI/GP for January 2027 and a 2024 Free software for research award. The documentation page was last modified 2026-09-29. The homepage footer still shows 'Last Modified: 2024-02-12', so that line is stale.
brief.caveats: Graphical plotting requires X11, which on macOS means installing XQuartz (per brew's caveat). gp2c handles only a subset of the GP language. The license is GPLv2 or later. The brew formula's executables include a versioned gp-2.17 binary, which may not match the current 2.19.0 release, so check the version you actually get. I did not run anything.

gp is an easy-to-use interactive shell giving access to the PARI functions.
gp2c-compiled scripts will typically run 3 or 4 times faster.

entry.title: PARI/GP
entry.tldr: A number theory calculator with its own small language, built in Bordeaux since the early 1980s, for factoring, elliptic curves and other exact arithmetic.
entry.deeper_look:
PARI/GP is a free computer algebra system aimed at fast computation in number theory: factorization, algebraic number theory, elliptic curves, modular forms, L-functions. It also handles matrices, polynomials, power series and many transcendental functions, plus numerical summation and integration.

You mostly meet it through `gp`, an interactive shell where you type expressions and get results back. The same shell runs scripts written in GP, the project's own small language. Underneath is PARI, a C library that does the heavy arithmetic, and `gp` is a front end exposing those functions.

The University of Bordeaux has developed it since the early 1980s. The homepage describes it as built for speed in number theory while also being free software under the GPL. That focus is the idea worth poking at: it is not trying to be a general symbolic algebra system, but a fast tool for working with integers, number fields and curves.

For scripts that need more speed, there is gp2c, a compiler from GP to C that loads the compiled functions back into `gp`. The homepage says compiled scripts typically run 3 or 4 times faster, though gp2c only understands a subset of GP.
entry.install:
brew install pari
# Graphical plotting needs X11 on macOS: brew install --cask xquartz
